# Podcasting for Small Businesses: Why & How to Start One

Learn how small businesses can utilise the power of podcasts to build loyal communities, brand awareness, industry authority, and more.

Written By:

![Camila Leme-Nelson from Cue.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/637cce16097f454270a7e17f/69fd9bf628e0ee0d39abdb1d_CAMILLA-LEME-NELSON-2026.avif)[

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/637cce16097f454270a7e17f/67126c999030c930beb72e12_small%20business.avif)

[![Black pause symbol with two vertical rounded bars on a white background.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/619d364fc1c71ac75b852b83/637cecbe010c802020e87eae_pause-button.avif)](https://www.cueproductions.com/post/podcasting-for-small-businesses#)[![White play button.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/619d364fc1c71ac75b852b83/62e28779cc33c7ed2eb3f934_Asset%202.svg)](https://www.cueproductions.com/post/podcasting-for-small-businesses#)

Listen in Full:

[![Apple Podcasts icon.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/619d364fc1c71ac75b852b83/6a0dcdc2673b044187531e1f_apple_podcasts.svg)](https://www.cueproductions.com/post/podcasting-for-small-businesses#)[![Spotify icon.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/619d364fc1c71ac75b852b83/6a0dcdc261b5a80d17c07817_spotify.svg)](https://www.cueproductions.com/post/podcasting-for-small-businesses#)

Your small business needs a podcast. Why? Because in today’s competitive market, [standing out](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/what-makes-a-good-podcast/) is more challenging than ever. Podcasts offer a unique, personal way to [connect](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/build-community-podcast/) with your [audience](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/podcast-audience/), build authority, and grow your brand.

This article outlines 12 reasons why starting a podcast could be the game-changer your small business needs - from boosting brand visibility to fostering stronger connections with your [audience](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/how-to-grow-your-podcast-audience/).

## 12 Reasons Why Your Small Business Needs a Podcast

Here’s 12 reasons why having a [podcast content strategy](https://www.cuepodcasts.com/post/podcast-content-strategy) might make sense for your small business. 

### 1\. Podcasting Is a Popular Medium

Podcasting is still on a growth trajectory worldwide. [By the end of 2024](https://www.demandsage.com/podcast-statistics/), the number of people listening to podcasts is expected to reach 504.9 million, an increase of 8.7% compared to 2023. On top of that, the [industry](https://backlinko.com/podcast-stats) is worth over 23 billion dollars as of 2023, but its growth is projected to increase to over 100 billion before 2030.

People worldwide are listening to podcasts, even [Gen Zers](https://www.demandsage.com/podcast-statistics/), who are discovering podcasting more than twice the rate of other ages and leading the way in podcast consumption.

Regardless of your niche, target audience, or industry, there is a space for you and your business in an industry that is not only growing but often less competitive and crowded than other marketing mediums.

### 2\. Establishes Authority in Your Field

Establishing authority in your industry can help your business gain trust and recognition. Podcasts allow you to do this by consistently sharing your expertise in a direct, personal format. The conversational nature of podcasts allows you to connect with your audience in a way that written content alone can't, making your expertise more relatable and engaging.

An example of this is [Azets UK](https://www.azets.co.uk/), a leading accounting and business advisory service provider, who launched the [_Bang the Drum_](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/bang-the-drum/id1654192554) podcast in partnership with [Cue Productions](https://www.cueproductions.com/). By offering practical advice tailored to SME owners, Azets UK effectively positioned itself as an authority in business growth and management. This podcast showcases their deep knowledge in these areas and reinforces their role as trusted advisors to small and medium-sized businesses.

![Bang the Drum podcast artwork.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/637cce16097f454270a7e17f/67126b965e2298877976c14e_67126ac59df0deae17b4fc0f_Bang%2520the%2520Drum%2520Artwork.avif)

Azets' Bang the Drum

### 3\. Creates Repurposable Content

As a business, creating content is key, but constantly figuring out what to post can be exhausting. That’s where podcasts come in - they’re like content goldmines. One episode can be turned into a [blog](https://www.cuepodcasts.com/post/podcast-vs-blog) post, [social media](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/how-to-promote-your-podcast-on-social-media/) clips, or even a [video](https://amplify.matchmaker.fm/podcast-audiograms/). This means you can reach different people on different platforms without reinventing the wheel every time. It’s a smart way to keep your brand active across channels while saving you time and energy.

[9 Ways to Repurpose Your Branded Podcast Content (Examples)](https://www.cuepodcasts.com/post/repurpose-podcast-content)

### 4\. Build Stronger Connections With Your Audience

Everything in your business starts and ends with your audience, and podcasting offers a unique way to connect with them. Podcasts allow listeners to engage with content in a personal and intimate setting, often when they are most focused - like commuting or exercising. [Research shows](https://deloitte.wsj.com/cmo/many-podcast-listeners-trust-hosts-feel-sense-of-community-survey-finds-1e873037) podcast listeners develop a deeper connection with hosts, as the consistent, conversational format creates a sense of familiarity and trust.

A strong example is the [_PeopleFirst Podcast_](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/peoplefirst-the-young-careers-podcast/id1676447770), by [Brook Street Recruitment](https://www.brookstreet.co.uk/), produced in collaboration with Cue. This podcast has a specific target audience - Gen Z and Millennial workers - offering targeted tips and advice for their specific needs. This allowed Brook Street Recruitment to position itself as a company that truly understands and values its audience’s needs - thus building a strong connection with listeners and [potential clients](https://www.cuepodcasts.com/post/generating-leads-from-a-podcast).

![PeopleFirst: The Young Careers Podcast show artwork.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/637cce16097f454270a7e17f/66ac9f38f7ef63b093df75ce_66ac9e995a20669f2b2c607a_peoplefirst-the-young-careers-podcast-brook-2uoXJ960mY7-eijX3Q8TLSA.1400x1400.avif)

# Podcast Advertising Strategies for Small Brands

Explore top LinkedIn content from expert professionals.

## Summary

Podcast advertising strategies for small brands focus on using audio content to build awareness, trust, and sales by tapping into loyal podcast audiences. This approach includes sponsoring podcast episodes, creating engaging audio series, and partnering with hosts to connect with listeners in a personal and memorable way.

*   **Craft authentic scripts**: Make sure your ad copy matches your brand’s voice and speaks directly to the audience so listeners stay engaged and receptive to your message.
*   **Launch audio series**: Consider releasing a limited podcast series or “audio album” across major platforms to boost your brand’s visibility and drive organic traffic without needing a long-term commitment.
*   **Secure exclusive sponsorships**: Partner with smaller podcasts as an exclusive sponsor for a set period to gain repeated exposure and build lasting audience trust, often at a lower cost than other advertising channels.

    If you’re going to be a podcaster, you need to learn the art of the ad script… Not only are they crucial to how the business makes money, but they also take a ton of time to create. My team averages half a day – maybe more sometimes – generating what amounts to about 15 minutes of ad copy. That’s crazy math… 4 -5 hours of input for 15 minutes of output. It’s not an easy code to crack. There’s nothing more droning than an ad that comes on in the middle of a pivotal part in the podcast that just feels painful to sit through. And I know you all know what I mean. There’s a finesse to it that HAS to be there in order for the audience to stay engaged and the overall messaging to be effective. You do want to drive listeners to your advertisers but not at the expense of their own UX. Here’s what I recommend: 👉 The copy has to sound like you. If it’s written in a way that doesn’t jive with your natural cadence or flow, it’ll sound clunky and ultimately be a waste of airtime. 👉 Engagement is crucial to success. A good rule of thumb here is write the copy in a way that enables you to talk WITH your audience, not AT them. 👉 Meeting them where they are is always going to be an easier sell. And this is where it’s helpful to promote products that you, yourself use. When you can own the sell, your audience will resonate with that and be much more inclined to try the product. 👉 Less is more. Keep them short and sweet. Remember that their connective experience has ultimately been interrupted to benefit your bottom line. Own that potential frustration and keep the disconnection time minimal. 👉 Infuse the script with personality when you read it. Don’t go monotone when you break for the ads. If you sound like you’re not into it, your audience won’t be either and the last thing you want is people tuning out your best sponsors that give you your predictable cashflow. Bonus points if you can make the ads so entertaining that people don't mind them, and might even look forward to your humor/personality during the reads (just make sure to stay brand-safe! Here’s looking at you, Bill Burr) 👉 And size does not matter here! Do good for even the smallest clients and they will continue to give you repeat (predictable) business. And even tell their network about their success with your podcast. But half-ass the script or botch the delivery and even the smallest client can cost you your big ones. Reputation is everything in this business. Don't half-ass it, no matter how tempting it might be sometimes.

# How Can Podcast Advertising Help Small, Local Businesses?

![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/74fd8493f6e4c0abaaa55e54ce38bdf1b5051a4a2d49702b2fc309b81a331686?s=100&d=identicon&r=g)

by [Jarrod Tennell](https://blog.podbean.com/author/jarrodt80c5041862/)

[August 28, 2018](https://blog.podbean.com/how-can-podcast-advertising-help-small-local-businesses/)

![Podcast Advertising Help Small, Local Businesses](https://i0.wp.com/blog.podbean.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/podcast-advertising-help-small-local-businesses1.jpg?resize=950%2C633&ssl=1)

Local media can play an important role in promoting small, local businesses. It can be a great way to target a narrow market with relevant messages. Many small businesses put advertising dollars toward local radio and newspapers. They may try billboards, flyers, local community boards or websites.

Small business owners need to be smart about their marketing and advertising efforts. Typically, they’ll be looking for effective, low-cost solutions but it can be hard to find that perfect combination. Sometimes local media exceeds the budget of a new or growing business. And, many businesses are finding that what’s worked in the past is no longer so effective. In recent years, many have turned to online advertising that allows targeting and provides delivery analytics. Another benefit is the simplicity and ease of getting campaigns running quickly.

Few local business owners will have considered podcast advertising. But now, some platforms are offering programmatic podcast advertising that targets only listeners in certain areas. So, podcasts can be a new form of local media for your small business to tap into. Fortunately, podcast advertising also has the potential to deliver more for less cost too. A small company can “sound big” without spending a lot. It’s a lot like what websites have done for small businesses in leveling the playing field.

#### Your Potential Customers Are Listening to Podcasts

According to [a report from Edison Research](http://www.adweek.com/news/technology/65-listeners-are-likely-buy-product-after-hearing-ad-podcast-173299), 21 percent of Americans (age 12+) will have listened to a podcast in the last month. To put that into perspective, that’s the same number of Americans who use Twitter and 8% more than use Spotify.

Podcasts tend to have affluent, educated audiences. 85% of podcast listeners have a college education and 36% make more than $75K/year.

#### Podcast Advertising Effectiveness

Research shows 62% of podcast listeners report making a purchase as a result of an ad they heard on a podcast. A study on NPR podcasts showed even higher results, with 75% of listeners taking action on a sponsored message. Podcast listeners are highly engaged, with 88% of them subscribing and listening to most or all episodes. Because podcasts are not heavily saturated with ads, listeners have high brand recall (over 70%).

#### New Technologies Increase Targeting and Ease

Programmatic ad buying now makes the process of purchasing podcast advertising much easier. A small business can buy ads directly, without a lengthy process or large ad budget necessary to work with an agency. The process is similar to setting up Google or Facebook ads (maybe even easier).

And, the technology now supports more targeting. So, for example, you can run ads to be served up only to listeners in your state or metro area. This effectively makes podcast advertising a new form of local media, but available on a smaller budget. For example, one recent campaign run via Podbean’s Ads system resulted in 100,000 targeted impressions for the business for $300.

To learn more about podcast advertising for your local business, [read more](https://sponsorship.podbean.com/). You can set up a campaign in minutes and give it a try! You set budget caps, and can modify or stop a campaign any time so it’s low risk with potential for high reward.

**Get a high return on investment for your small business: get started with [Ads today](https://sponsorship.podbean.com/).**
